notes: Historical revenue and operating income (EBIT) are taken from Alphabet FY2023-2025 consolidated statements of income in the FY2025 Form 10-K. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))

D&A is operationalized as depreciation of property and equipment from the consolidated statements of cash flows (amortization of intangibles is not explicitly separable as a single 'D&A' line item in the cash-flow section used here). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))

NWC is defined as (Accounts receivable + Other current assets) - (Accounts payable + Accrued compensation and benefits + Accrued expenses and other current liabilities + Accrued revenue share + Deferred revenue), i.e., net working capital excluding cash and securities, which can be negative at Alphabet due to deferred revenue/payables dynamics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204425000014/goog-20241231.htm))

Tax rate (0.16), WACC (0.085), terminal growth (0.03), terminal EV/EBITDA exit multiple (18.0), and NOL utilization percent (0.25) are base-case modeling assumptions rather than explicitly stated in the filing.

current_price is set to an implied per-share value derived from the market cap snapshot and the FY2025 consolidated diluted share denominator to avoid share-class reconciliation issues for GOOG vs consolidated EPS share counts. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))

Investments in the assumptions include marketable + non-marketable securities from the balance sheet (excluding equity-method detail not separately decomposed for this pipeline), which is a modeling choice; if your pipeline instead treats some securities as non-operating excluded from 'investments', adjust accordingly. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Continued AI-driven product improvements that increase advertiser ROI and improve cloud attachment/consumption growth.

Progress on planned acquisitions, including Wiz (expected close in 2026) and Intersect (expected close in 1H 2026), which could accelerate cloud security/data infrastructure capabilities. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))
Evidence of easing capex intensity without impairing revenue growth, improving forward free-cash-flow conversion.
company_overview: Alphabet is organized by Google Services, Google Cloud, and Other Bets segments.
Revenues are generated primarily from online advertising, cloud-based solutions, and subscriptions/platforms/devices.

FY2025 operating margin was ~0.32, indicating strong operating profitability and monetization leverage across its ad and cloud businesses. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 revenues were $402,836,000,000 and operating income (EBIT) was $129,039,000,000. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))

FY2025 capex (purchases of property and equipment) was $91,447,000,000 and depreciation of property and equipment was $21,136,000,000, consistent with ongoing technical infrastructure buildout. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))

Alphabet had net operating loss carryforwards totaling approximately $41,000,000,000 (federal/state/foreign combined). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth decelerates gradually from recent mid-teens levels toward low-double-digit/upper-single-digit by 2030, reflecting mature ad and cloud expansion while still scaling monetization.

EBIT margin is assumed to stabilize near the recent ~0.32 level, supported by operating leverage and sustained advertising efficiency. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity normalizes over the forecast period as the post-2025 infrastructure spend scales from peak investment toward steadier maintenance/expansion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))
Negative net working capital (excluding cash/securities) implies structural cash conversion support as deferred revenue and payables outpace receivables within the selected NWC definition.
key_risks: Ad demand cyclicality and increased traffic acquisition/content costs could pressure margins versus the base case.
Sustained elevated capex could reduce free cash flow or lead to lower-than-expected operating leverage.

Regulatory and legal developments (fines/settlements, antitrust remedies) could impact costs and growth expectations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000018/goog-20251231.htm))
